title: The Door Left Open
stanzas: The key was still in the lock,
so the door never really closed.
All afternoon the hallway light
lay in a yellow stripe across the tiles.
I could hear the neighbours' television
through the gap, and their kettle,
and once a plate went down too hard
and somebody laughed and said sorry.
The fan turned. The curtains breathed.
A fly found the kitchen and stayed.
I kept the door open for the air,
not for you, I told myself.
At six the building smelled of onions.
At eight the stairs went quiet.
I put the chain on, then took it off,
then put the chain on again.
When your steps came up the last flight
I was already at the table,
reading the same page,
and the door was open, and I said nothing about it.
